doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Subbing for Johnny Hodges in the Ellington band
summary: In 1969 he was called while at Minton's to sub for the ill Hodges, possibly through Stanley Dance, and impressed Cootie by reading the sacred concert music.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Which is a combination of blues and — So you were with Ray Charles, and in 1969 you started subbing for Johnny Hodges?

Yeah. He was out about two weeks. And I was working at Minton’s then I remember, and they called me up there, I was working with a small band. And they called me at Minton’s and they said Johnny was going to be sick. Because I think probably Stanley Dance had something to do with it. You know Stanley Dance, don’t you?
Yeah. So he’s the one that may have recommended you?
Well you were certainly aware of Johnny Hodges for many years before that. How did you feel stepping into his place?
I had no feelings about it at all. It was just a gig. I figured I’d be gone in two weeks and coming back home. But I never was frightened or nothing like that.
Yeah? Well good. Did the rest of the orchestra, were they supportive of you in that position?

Yeah I think so. You know the second night I was with them they played a sacred concert, and I never heard that music before. So they pulled all this music out. So I read it, Cootie was sitting right behind me and said, “Man, that boy can read.”
Yeah. Because a lot of those fellows just had the charts all memorized, right?
